checks: The order interval of finite positive measures dominated by E is weakly compact on the common compact support. Borel Radon–Nikodym densities in [0,1] describe it exactly. Positive mandatory mass keeps normalization continuous.

The displayed coefficient a=tT₂/[tT₂+(1−t)T₁] gives tT₁T₂ divided by the common denominator as the first unnormalized weight. Renormalizing yields the prescribed convex combination of barycenters, including t=0 and t=1.

For fixed R, maximizing the unnormalized signed numerator selects exactly its positive part, and minimizing selects exactly its negative part. Both functions are continuous and strictly decreasing at rate at least A, with opposite limits. The root identifies and attains each support value.
Every normalized candidate measure contains L/(A+B), of mass A/(A+B). Each residual barycenter lies in K, so the common translate of (B/(A+B))K gives the width bound, including B=0.
